title: Rapid Exploratory Maps and their potential role in supporting evidence-to-policy dialogues and processes
abstract: arXiv:2611.31693v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Producing useful evidence syntheses requires clearly formulated research questions linked to an understanding of their optimal scope. When policymakers (or other end users) commission or steer the production of systematic reviews or other evidence syntheses to fulfil a demand for evidence, these parameters are rarely specified sufficiently for production to proceed. Instead, these details are typically developed via a collaborative dialogic process involving evidence producers and users to ensure the resulting synthesis will meet users' needs. This process is informed by scoping and (more-or-less formally) mapping the existing evidence base, which can take many weeks or months, slowed by applying mostly manual processes to identify and characterise the evidence. translated_title: 快速探索性证据图谱及其在支持证据向政策转化对话与过程中的潜在作用
translated_abstract: 产出有用的证据综合（evidence syntheses）需要明确提出的研究问题，并与对其最佳范围的理解相关联。当政策制定者（或其他最终用户）为了满足对证据的需求而委托或指导系统综述或其他证据综合的生产时，这些参数很少被充分明确地规定到足以使生产得以进行的程度。相反，这些细节通常是通过证据生产者和使用者之间协作对话的过程来制定的，以确保最终产出的证据综合能够满足使用者的需求。这一过程依赖于对现有证据库的范围界定和（或多或少正式的）证据图谱绘制，而这可能需要数周甚至数月的时间，且由于主要依靠人工流程来识别和描述证据而进展缓慢。人工智能（AI）技术的最新发展为更快速、迭代和响应式地绘制相关证据图谱开辟了新的机遇，以支持……
tldr: 该论文提出利用人工智能技术构建快速探索性证据图谱，大幅缩短证据图谱绘制所需的时间，从而支持证据生产者与政策制定者之间的协作对话，更高效地确定证据综合的研究问题与范围。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes leveraging AI technologies to rapidly generate exploratory evidence maps, dramatically shortening the time needed to map existing evidence bases and thereby supporting collaborative dialogues between evidence producers and policymakers in defining research questions and scopes for evidence syntheses.
